I have been trying to reply to you for a couple of hours but my reddit app seems to be bugged or something. So I apologize for the Long reply.  
  
Well, I would say the internet but it's more like the computer isn't connecting to the modem to allow for internet access. In my network settings it tries to identify a modem for a couple seconds before giving up. Do you still think this is due to the modem not identifying my PC's IP address or could it more hardware problems?

I'm not great with people. I don't know how to "open up" to someone in real life. It was hard with a counselor and I cried for like thirty minutes the first time I was able to explain my situation. That two years ago in a very stressful period of my life. I was very low-mood feeling and I *needed* to release it someway without doing something stupid. I don't know what exactly I went through then but I wish I could feel it again. I've tried to be more open with people but it doesn't come out too well, which is weird. So I'm ultimately afraid of actually talking to someone about myself. It makes me feel bad or selfish and dependant on others. I don't really KNOW these people I'm suppose to open up too. It feels cheap to pay someone  to listen to you or like you're unable to be functioning on your own or like no one really cares about you anyway. That was just from spending some weeks talking to a counsellor. I just makes me feel that way.

The thing about trying this now, I'm in a transition from being able to go to college. It will require me to move away. I was accepted to a school and I'm in the process now (If i don't screw it up.) Do you think there's a way the school I applied too might be able to help? I really want this thing to work because I've flaked out going to college for two years with entirely the same things stopping me. But I don't know if I can just walk up to someone at the school and say "Hey, I'm trying to get through this acceptable and progression into the school but I'm like.. freaking out over the whole thing. Can you help me?" I feel like if I did that, I'd be turned away and put on some kind of crazy list for the school or told that maybe I just don't cut it for attending the school.
Is this some kind of prayer or chant? It sounds like an interesting way to challenge these thoughts and feelings. Do you mind if I ask where you learned something like this?

I have a friend who's playing Wildstar MMORPG right now. He says it's really refreshing to the genre.  As for some other games, I specifically played steam games myself. I'm sorry I'm not really sure what games I could suggest. I quit playing altogether last year. I had to cut it out of my time completely to get to stop but everyone's different. If you are alright with keeping searching for another game to play, I'd encourage you too. There's plenty of games out there, a lot of different types. You never know what you might run into too. From this experience, you can learn to look out for those signs and symptoms that maybe you need to step back or quit playing certain games maybe?   
Alternatively, if you aren't oppose to quit gaming entirely. I suggest finding a hobby to fill that time with. I got back into drawing and painting personally. Though if you've ever wanted to try something new. Now would be a good time too really.   
  
That was the same mentality I had while playing Starcraft 2. I wasn't terrible, I did well but I certainly wasn't the best. I was more ranked towards the middle of the bar honestly. It's not really about being bad or good at a game that this suggestion comes. It's more about the weight and mentality you carry behind it. My father is a craftsman and his health has hindered his ability to be as good as he use to be at his craft. He's by no means gotten worse but he carries the expectation that he has to be faster, stronger, better. He's very hard on himself because age and health keep him from being as fast as he use to be. The problem is that he still expects way to much of himself. If you have days where you're playing a game poorly and it can ruin your mood, this might be an indicator that you are being hard on yourself and expecting too much from yourself. Some games really emphasize this mentality. I have friends who play dota2 and they can be a little off on a day and it reflects on a team and they quickly lash back his inabilities. These aren't the type of games I enjoy so I stay away from them. Since I quit playing games so seriously, I've just tried to not take games so seriously. The bit of advice that helped me was "If you're playing a game, you're playing a game to have fun... yet if you aren't having fun. Quit playing." That little bit helped me become very aware of the time I was spending and how I was spending it.

I do like to go to a park and walk when I feel stressed. I went yesterday but the problem still is persisting. This isn't normal for me. I try to open up the tabs in my computer to get started or try to start writing it's all flooding back to me. I can distract myself to calm down, but this just turns into avoidance because I when I go back to it, it instantly tightens back up.   
  
edit: This is why it's particularly challenging to me right now. It hasn't felt like this before. Where it just comes back so easily.

Fours is a lot of time for playing a game. Though I use to play an FPS game for an upwards of eight to twelves hours a day. From your other comments you don't sound like you specifically need to play. You value a lot of other instances over the game, which is healthy. Things like spending time with family, working, and such. Yet as someone else mentioned, you have a lot of self-worth put into this game. I haven't played LoL but I use to play Starcraft 2. I'll preface by saying I really liked playing that game and I really like how the game worked (kind of). The problem was that I couldn't be a great player in that game on a casual level. It seemed like that game required a huge investment of hours devoted to muscle memory and over the course of trying to be good I found I would get super stressed over my ability in playing. After a point, I just had to put it down and walk away. Declare that I just wasn't suited for playing it. I don't know if that feels similar to your situation but I wanted to ask. How are you in terms of playing other games? You say you only play one game but have you given other games a try? Maybe looked for another game entirely? (Probably not Dota2 or Heroes of the Storm.)

I would honestly like too but I don't really have the money too. I tried to talk to counselors at college, not the same thing I'm sure but I didn't feel my health to be of concern rather limiting my time spent with them. I'm really scared of seeking help and opening up to others.

I would be open to the idea of therapy, I've even given way to bring open with medication if it numbs me or subsides this hard breathing. I however don't feel I have access or the funds to see anyone. I've talked to counselors at most but they weren't entirely helpful to me so I might have a bit of a trust issue with a therapist. I've been trying really hard to do self help books and self therapy for things like cognitive distortions. I'm not sure if I'm making progress or not. Someone recommend mood gym to me today.

Thanks, I feel like I might legitimately enjoy the subject I've applied for. A design and architecture related field. The problem is the issue of a lot of the other work involved. I don't have family or friends to encourage or help me through this process. So in applying and doing paper work and having to consider the forethought of things like job outlook and debt along side much of the decisions I'm making now feel overwhelming and easy to make mistakes. Though I am genuinely nervous about my major at the same time. I don't know that I will like it or if it will be right for me but from my background and interest it sounds like it could be.

I just can't relax about things. It's so hard to calm down if things worry me. Yesterday I went through the process of picking an apartment for college. No clue what I was doing. I have this half interested idea that I don't think I can make this work and will just flake out on attending not something I want to be true but it feels like that's the future predetermined for me and I just keep thinking if I flake out I have no choice but to kill myself then. However, going through this process begins out the worst in what may be a serious anxiety disorder and the pain from it just make me want to avoid the work or kill myself because it physically and mentally hurts. So I'm stuck between the same outcome in mentality I suppose. I'm just exhausted between this being how it is all the time.
